'''The Institute and Faculty of Actuaries''' ('''IFoA''') is the United Kingdom's chartered professional body for actuaries. It represents and regulates more than 34,000 members worldwide and works internationally through offices in London, Oxford and Edinburgh and regional offices in Beijing, Malaysia and Singapore.<ref>{{cite web |title=About our membership – Facts and figures |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/about-us/about-our-membership-facts-and-figures/ |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Visit us |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/visit-us/ |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref> The profession is overseen in the UK by the [[Financial Reporting Council]] (FRC), which sets technical actuarial standards and monitors the IFoA's regulation of actuaries.<ref>{{cite web |title=Actuarial |url=https://www.frc.org.uk/library/standards-codes-policy/actuarial/ |website=Financial Reporting Council |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref> The IFoA was created in 2010 by the merger of the [[Institute of Actuaries]] (founded 1848) and the [[Faculty of Actuaries]] (founded 1856).<ref>{{cite web |title=Constitution: Charter, bye-laws, rules and regulations |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/about-us/governance-and-structure/constitution/ |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref> In November 2024 the IFoA introduced the ''Chartered Actuary'' designation for Fellow and Associate members.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chartered actuary designation introduced for IFoA-qualified actuaries |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/news-and-media-releases/media-releases-and-statements/2024/nov/12-nov-24-chartered-actuary-designation-introduced-for-ifoa-qualified-actuaries/ |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |date=12 November 2024 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref>

==History==
The IFoA came into being on 1 August 2010 following the merger of the Institute of Actuaries and the Faculty of Actuaries in Scotland. The merger was implemented by amendments to the Institute's Royal Charter and accompanying governance documents, with the combined body assuming the assets and liabilities of the former organisations.<ref>{{cite web |title=Constitution: Charter, bye-laws, rules and regulations |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/about-us/governance-and-structure/constitution/ |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref>

==Structure and governance==
The IFoA is incorporated by Royal Charter and governed by a Council which delegates to a board and a system of policy and regulatory committees.<ref>{{cite web |title=Constitution: Charter, bye-laws, rules and regulations |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/about-us/governance-and-structure/constitution/ |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Finance and governance report 2023–24 |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/document-library/about-us/annual-reports/annual-report-2023-2024/finance-and-governance-report-23-24/ |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |date=2024 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref>

Regulatory oversight is split between the profession and the UK's Financial Reporting Council (FRC). The FRC sets and maintains technical actuarial standards and oversees the IFoA's regulation of actuaries, including through its Actuarial Monitoring Programme.<ref>{{cite web |title=Actuarial |url=https://www.frc.org.uk/library/standards-codes-policy/actuarial/ |website=Financial Reporting Council |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Actuarial Monitoring Programme |url=https://www.frc.org.uk/library/standards-codes-policy/actuarial/actuarial-monitoring-programme/ |website=Financial Reporting Council |date=7 April 2025 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref> The IFoA's regulatory board includes a significant proportion of lay (non-actuary) members.<ref>{{cite web |title=Regulatory Board annual report 2022–23 |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/media/zhok5zpe/regulatory-board-annual-report-2022-23.pdf |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |date=October 2023 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref>

The IFoA Foundation is the profession's registered charity, supporting scholarships, mentoring and [[widening participation]] initiatives in the UK and internationally.<ref>{{cite web |title=IFoA Foundation |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/about-us/ifoa-foundation/ |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=The IFoA Foundation (SC049518) |url=https://www.oscr.org.uk/about-charities/search-the-register/charity-details?number=SC049518 |website=Office of the Scottish Charity Regulator |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref>

==President==
{{As of|2025|07}}, the president of the Institute and Faculty of Actuaries is Paul Sweeting, who began a two-year term in July 2025, succeeding Kartina Tahir Thomson.<ref>{{cite web |title=Paul Sweeting becomes IFoA president |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/news/paul-sweeting-becomes-ifoa-president/ |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |date=10 July 2025 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Paul Sweeting – President of the IFoA |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/about-us/governance-and-structure/honorary-officers-and-the-chief-executive-officer-of-the-ifoa/paul-sweeting/ |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref>

==Research and data==
The IFoA supports the [[Continuous Mortality Investigation]] (CMI), which provides mortality and morbidity experience analyses and practical tools widely used by actuaries. The CMI Mortality Projections Model is updated regularly; Working Paper 201 introduced ''CMI_2024'' in June 2025, calibrated to population data to 31 December 2024.<ref>{{cite web |title=Continuous Mortality Investigation – overview |url=https://www.actuaries.org.uk/learn-and-develop/continuous-mortality-investigation |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Mortality projections |url=https://www.actuaries.org.uk/learn-and-develop/continuous-mortality-investigation/cmi-investigations/mortality-projections |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |date=June 2025 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=CMI Working Paper 201: CMI_2024 |url=https://www.actuaries.org.uk/learn-and-develop/continuous-mortality-investigation/cmi-working-papers/mortality-projections/cmi-working-paper-201 |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |date=2025 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref> The CMI also publishes regular mortality monitors for [[England and Wales]] and periodic updates on recent experience.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mortality monitor |url=https://www.actuaries.org.uk/learn-and-develop/continuous-mortality-investigation/other-cmi-outputs/mortality-monitor |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Record low summer mortality, says CMI |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/news-and-media-releases/media-releases-and-statements/2025/oct/08-oct-25-record-low-summer-mortality-says-cmi/ |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |date=8 October 2025 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref>

The IFoA’s research and thought-leadership activity has been repositioned in recent years, with the Actuarial Research Centre (ARC) closed and resources focused on member-led and industry-collaboration projects.<ref>{{cite web |title=Research |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/thought-leadership/research/ |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref>

==Regulation and standards==
All members are bound by the ''Actuaries’ Code'', which sets core professional principles. Version 3.2 of the Code took effect on 25 September 2025, accompanied by updated guidance.<ref>{{cite web |title=Q&A: Changes to the Actuaries’ Code, 2025 |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/standards/standards-and-guidance/the-actuaries-code/qa-changes-to-the-actuaries-code-2025/ |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |date=25 September 2025 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Revised Actuaries’ Code and guidance now in effect |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/news/revised-actuaries-code-and-guidance-now-in-effect/ |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |date=25 September 2025 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref>

Within the UK geographic scope, members must also comply with the FRC’s ''Technical Actuarial Standards'' (TASs), including TAS 100 (General) and the relevant Specific TASs (for example TAS 200: Insurance; TAS 300: Pensions; TAS 400: Funeral Plans).<ref>{{cite web |title=Actuarial |url=https://www.frc.org.uk/library/standards-codes-policy/actuarial/ |website=Financial Reporting Council |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Principles for Technical Actuarial Work (guidance on TAS 100) |url=https://www.actuaries.org.uk/documents/principles-technical-actuarial-work-guidance-application-technical-actuarial-standard-100 |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref>

The IFoA operates the Quality Assurance Scheme (QAS) for organisations employing actuaries; as at 31 October 2024 there were 42 accredited organisations, with additional firms covered by the QAS CPD scheme.<ref>{{cite web |title=QAS Committee annual report (Regulatory Board papers) |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/media/0p3bbqyc/paper_07_00_item_062_noting_qas-committee-annual-report.pdf |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |date=July 2025 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref> It also acts as a Designated Professional Body under Part XX of the [[Financial services|Financial Services]] and Markets Act 2000, licensing firms for certain exempt regulated activities.<ref>{{cite web |title=Designated Professional Body (overview) |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/standards/designated-professional-body/ |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=DPB Handbook and Guide |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/standards/designated-professional-body/dpb-handbook-and-guide/ |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref>

==Education and qualifications==
The IFoA’s qualification structure (introduced with ''Curriculum 2019'') comprises Core Principles (CS1–CS2, CM1–CM2, CB1–CB3), Core Practices (CP1–CP3), Specialist Principles (SP) and Specialist Advanced (SA) subjects. Personal and Professional Development (PPD) and professional skills training are also required.<ref>{{cite web |title=Curriculum |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/curriculum/ |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Fellowship |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/membership/types-of-membership/fellowship/ |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Personal and Professional Development (PPD) |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/qualify/personal-and-professional-development/ |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref>

Since 2019 new students normally qualify first as Associates before progressing to Fellowship, aligning Associateship with international standards.<ref>{{cite web |title=Qualification handbook 2022–23 |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/media/2bvpngbv/qualification-handbook-2022-23.pdf |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |date=2022 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref> University accreditation and exemptions are available through recognised programmes.<ref>{{cite web |title=University courses with exemptions (Route A) |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/qualify/exam-exemptions/university-courses-with-exemptions-route-a/ |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref>

In 2024 the IFoA introduced the ''Chartered Actuary'' designation for Fellows and Associates; members can adopt the designation after meeting the eligibility criteria and remain subject to IFoA standards.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chartered actuary designation introduced for IFoA-qualified actuaries |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/news-and-media-releases/media-releases-and-statements/2024/nov/12-nov-24-chartered-actuary-designation-introduced-for-ifoa-qualified-actuaries/ |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |date=12 November 2024 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Chartered Actuary – overview |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/chartered/ |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref>

==Membership==
The IFoA reports a global membership of more than 34,000 actuaries and students.<ref>{{cite web |title=About our membership – Facts and figures |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/about-us/about-our-membership-facts-and-figures/ |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref> In 2024 the IFoA established new member committees in [[Greater China]] and the Middle East to support regional engagement.<ref>{{cite web |title=IFoA establishes the Greater China Committee |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/news-and-media-releases/news-articles/2024/dec/30-dec-24-ifoa-establishes-the-greater-china-committee/ |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |date=30 December 2024 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=IFoA launches new Middle East Member Committee |url=https://actuaries.org.uk/news-and-media-releases/news-articles/2024/dec/16-dec-24-ifoa-launches-new-middle-east-member-committee/ |website=Institute and Faculty of Actuaries |date=16 December 2024 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref>

==Public policy and scrutiny==
Following government reviews of audit and actuarial oversight, the UK Government confirmed in 2022 its intention to place the FRC’s oversight and regulation of the actuarial profession on a statutory footing as part of wider reforms (with the proposed Audit, Reporting and Governance Authority).<ref>{{cite web |title=Restoring trust in audit and corporate governance: government response |url=https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6294ab378fa8f5039107d54d/restoring-trust-in-audit-and-corporate-governance-govt-response.pdf |website=Department for Business, Energy & Industrial Strategy |date=1 June 2022 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref> The FRC’s monitoring and standard-setting activities for actuarial work continue alongside the IFoA’s own regulatory programme.<ref>{{cite web |title=Actuarial |url=https://www.frc.org.uk/library/standards-codes-policy/actuarial/ |website=Financial Reporting Council |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref>

In the wake of gilt-market stress in September–October 2022, commentators and parliamentary committees examined the role of liability-driven investment (LDI) strategies used by UK defined benefit schemes. Correspondence from the [[Bank of England]] described vulnerabilities and emergency measures taken during the period, and [[House of Lords]] committees took evidence on LDI oversight and [[market structure]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Letter from Jon Cunliffe – LDI (5 October 2022) |url=https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/letter/2022/october/letter-from-jon-cunliffe-ldi-5-october-2022 |website=Bank of England |date=5 October 2022 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Letter from Jon Cunliffe – LDI (18 October 2022) |url=https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/letter/2022/october/letter-from-jon-cunliffe-ldi-18-october-2022.pdf |website=Bank of England |date=18 October 2022 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Defined benefit pensions with Liability Driven Investments |url=https://committees.parliament.uk/publications/40577/documents/197895/default/ |website=House of Lords Economic Affairs Committee |date=23 June 2023 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref> A range of views on lessons for actuaries and pension governance were expressed at the time, including in letters to the editor of national media.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.ft.com/content/6c226693-2128-4dc8-8df3-8ee4452de4c4 |title=Questions for actuaries in the LDI pensions debacle |work=Financial Times |date=3 October 2022 |access-date=13 October 2025 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

==Publications and media==
The IFoA’s monthly membership magazine is ''The Actuary'', published in print and online by Redactive Media Group on the IFoA’s behalf.<ref>{{cite web |title=A new website for The Actuary |url=https://redactive.co.uk/news/a-new-website-for-the-actuary/ |website=Redactive |date=2019 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=The Actuary magazine |url=https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.presspadapp.theactuarymagazine |website=Google Play |date=2 June 2025 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=The Actuary magazine – company page |url=https://uk.linkedin.com/company/the-actuary-magazine |website=LinkedIn |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref>
